[issue-triage] Rewrite skill in Python + add auto-triage agentic workflow (#3704)

[issue-triage] Rewrite skill in Python + add auto-triage agentic workflow (#3704)

The issue-triage skill relied on a cache branch for storing triage results and
used PowerShell scripts that only ran on Windows. The report output was a single
JSON file with no human-readable companion.

~~ Skill rewrite ~~

Replace all PowerShell scripts with Python equivalents and switch from the cache
branch to direct `gh` CLI / GitHub MCP calls for fetching issue data:

  * render-triage-report.py + Jinja2 template produce triple output: JSON,
    Markdown, and a standalone HTML viewer (same pattern as security-audit and
    review-skia-update skills)
  * persist-triage.py writes artifacts to issue-triage-workspace/
  * validate-triage.py gates persistence on schema conformance
  * Renumber skill phases 1–6 with consistent sub-numbering; merge workaround
    validation into Phase 4 instead of a separate phase

Removed: issue-to-markdown.ps1, persist-triage.ps1, validate-triage.ps1

~~ Auto-triage agentic workflow ~~

Add `.github/workflows/auto-triage.md` — a gh-aw workflow with manual
`workflow_dispatch` trigger (takes an issue number). The agent runs the
issue-triage skill, then applies results through safe-outputs:

  * Labels (classification, visible on issue): type/*, area/*, os/*,
    backend/*, tenet/*, partner/*, triage/triaged
  * Project fields (analytical, visible on board only): Severity,
    Suggested Action, Confidence, Repro Quality, Error Type, Triage Summary

Labels and project fields have zero overlap — classification goes to labels,
analytical data goes to the SkiaSharp Backlog project board (mono/projects/1).

Requires repo secret `GH_AW_WRITE_PROJECT_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with org
project write scope) for the update-project safe-output.

~~ Eval suite ~~

Add evals/evals.json with 3 test cases (#3420, #3428, #3391) covering bug,
enhancement, and regression paths — 9 assertions total.

md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+---
+description: "Triage a SkiaSharp issue: classify, label, and update the backlog project board."
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      issue_number:
+        description: "Issue number to triage"
+        required: true
+        type: string
+  skip-bots: [github-actions, copilot, dependabot]
+  roles: all
+tools:
+  github:
+    toolsets: [issues]
+  bash: ["gh", "python3", "pip3", "jq"]
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - python
+safe-outputs:
+  add-labels:
+    allowed:
+      - "type/*"
+      - "area/*"
+      - "os/*"
+      - "backend/*"
+      - "tenet/*"
+      - "partner/*"
+      - "triage/triaged"
+    blocked: ["~*"]
+    max: 10
+    target: "*"
+  update-project:
+    project: "https://github.com/orgs/mono/projects/1"
+    max: 1
+    github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_AW_WRITE_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
+---
+
+# Auto-Triage SkiaSharp Issue
+
+Triage issue **#${{ github.event.inputs.issue_number }}** using the issue-triage skill, then apply labels and update the SkiaSharp Backlog project board.
+
+## Step 1 — Run the issue-triage skill
+
+Read and follow the instructions in `.agents/skills/issue-triage/SKILL.md` to triage issue #${{ github.event.inputs.issue_number }}.
+
+Complete all phases (Setup → Investigate → Analyze → Workarounds → Validate → Persist).
+
+After Phase 6 completes, the triage JSON will be at `issue-triage-workspace/${{ github.event.inputs.issue_number }}.json`.
+
+## Step 2 — Apply labels from classification
+
+Read the triage JSON file and extract the classification labels. Apply each label to the issue:
+
+- `classification.type.value` — the issue type label (e.g. `type/bug`)
+- `classification.area.value` — the component area label (e.g. `area/SkiaSharp`)
+- Each entry in `classification.platforms[]` — platform labels (e.g. `os/Android`)
+- Each entry in `classification.backends[]` — backend labels (e.g. `backend/Metal`)
+- Each entry in `classification.tenets[]` — quality tenet labels (e.g. `tenet/compatibility`)
+- `classification.partner` — partner label if present (e.g. `partner/maui`)
+
+After applying classification labels, also add the `triage/triaged` label to mark the issue as processed.
+
+Only apply labels that are non-null and non-empty. Skip any classification field that is absent or null.
+
+## Step 3 — Update project board fields
+
+Read the triage JSON and update the issue in the **SkiaSharp Backlog** project (https://github.com/orgs/mono/projects/1) with these custom fields:
+
+| Project Field | JSON Path | Notes |
+|--------------|-----------|-------|
+| Severity | `evidence.bugSignals.severity` | SINGLE_SELECT: critical, high, medium, low. Skip if null. |
+| Suggested Action | `output.actionability.suggestedAction` | SINGLE_SELECT: needs-investigation, close-as-fixed, etc. |
+| Confidence | `output.actionability.confidence` | NUMBER: 0.0–1.0. |
+| Repro Quality | `evidence.bugSignals.reproQuality` | SINGLE_SELECT: complete, partial, none. Skip if null. |
+| Error Type | `evidence.bugSignals.errorType` | SINGLE_SELECT: crash, exception, wrong-output, etc. Skip if null. |
+| Triage Summary | `analysis.summary` | TEXT: root cause hypothesis. Truncate to 1024 chars. |
+
+The `update-project` safe output auto-creates missing SINGLE_SELECT options — no need to pre-create values.
+
+Use `content_type: "issue"` and `content_number: ${{ github.event.inputs.issue_number }}` to identify the item.
+
+Only include fields that have non-null values in the triage JSON. Omit any field where the source value is null or absent.

Fix auto-triage: set min-integrity=none for public issue access (#3706)

* Fix auto-triage: set min-integrity=none for public issue access

On public repos, gh-aw automatically applies min-integrity=approved which
filters out issue content authored by non-collaborators. Since the triage
workflow needs to read issues from any community user, explicitly set
min-integrity=none and allowed-repos=all in the GitHub MCP tools config.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Scope allowed-repos to mono/skiasharp and mono/skia

Least-privilege: restrict the agent's GitHub MCP access to only the
repos it needs instead of 'all'. Patterns must be lowercase per gh-aw
guard policy validation.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add google/skia to allowed-repos for upstream issue lookup

The triage skill checks upstream Skia for related bugs and C++ header
capabilities. Adding google/skia lets the agent access those issues
through GitHub MCP.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Add gh-aw agent config and actions lock (#3709)

* Add gh-aw agent config and actions lock

Adds the agentic-workflows agent definition and actions lock file
generated by gh-aw init/upgrade. Updates .gitattributes to mark
lock.yml files as generated.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add hourly schedule trigger to auto-triage workflow

The workflow now runs on a cron schedule (every hour) in addition to
manual dispatch. On scheduled runs it finds the newest open issue
without a triage/triaged label that was created more than 1 hour ago,
giving reporters time to edit before the bot triages. If no matching
issue exists, the run exits cleanly.

Manual dispatch still works — pass an issue number explicitly, or leave
it blank to use the same auto-select logic.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add skip-if-no-match guard to auto-triage frontmatter

Uses gh-aw's native skip-if-no-match to fast-exit scheduled runs
when every open issue already has triage/triaged. This avoids
spinning up the agent when there's nothing to do.

The 1-hour age filter still lives in the body because GitHub search
doesn't support relative date math.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use schedule: hourly shorthand for scattered cron

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Move issue selection to on.steps pre-activation pattern

Uses the gh-aw on.steps: + on.permissions: + if: pattern from
the deterministic-agentic-patterns guide. The find-issue step
runs in the pre-activation job, and the agent is gated on
find-issue_result == 'success'. The issue number flows via
jobs.pre-activation.outputs into env.ISSUE_NUMBER for the agent.

This avoids burning agent compute when there's nothing to triage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use GitHub search created:< syntax instead of jq date filtering

Push the 'older than 1 hour' filter into the gh search query with
created:<${CUTOFF} so GitHub does the date filtering server-side.
This drops the jq post-processing, fetches only 1 result instead
of 50, and uses --jq for inline extraction.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use GNU date syntax for GitHub Actions (Ubuntu)

Actions runners are Ubuntu — use 'date -d' directly instead of
the macOS 'date -v' with fallback.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: pass issue number via needs.pre_activation.outputs in prompt

Remove /tmp/gh-aw/agent/ file approach. Use needs.pre_activation.outputs.issue_number
directly in the markdown body — this is permitted per gh-aw templating docs and gets
compiled into GH_AW_NEEDS_PRE_ACTIVATION_OUTPUTS_ISSUE_NUMBER env vars in the agent job.

Fixes the CI failure caused by workflow-level env: referencing needs context.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: remove --sort/--order flags from gh issue list

gh issue list doesn't support --sort. Use sort:created-asc in the
GitHub search query instead to pick the oldest untriaged issue.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: use sort:comments-desc for issue selection

Prioritize issues with more community engagement.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: use sort:reactions-desc for issue selection

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* revert: back to sort:comments-desc for issue selection

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: run auto-triage every 30 minutes

Keep the 1-hour age filter so new issues have time to settle before triage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
[auto-triage] Upload triage reports (JSON/MD/HTML) to agent artifact (#3711)

* Add Step 4 to copy triage reports into agent artifact

The issue-triage skill produces .json, .md, and .html files in
output/ai/repos/mono-SkiaSharp/ai-triage/. Add a step instructing the
agent to copy all three into /tmp/gh-aw/agent/ so they are included
in the workflow's agent artifact for downstream consumption.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Write triage markdown to step summary for in-UI viewing

Append the rendered markdown report to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so the
triage results are visible directly on the Actions run summary page
without downloading artifacts.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use literal /tmp/gh-aw/agent-step-summary.md path for step summary

The agent's bash resolves $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY to the runner's real
path which is inaccessible from inside the sandbox. Use the literal
/tmp/gh-aw/agent-step-summary.md path that gh-aw reads after the
agent finishes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use symlink redirect to write triage markdown to step summary

The agent sandbox blocks direct writes to /tmp/gh-aw/agent-step-summary.md but
allows writes to /tmp/gh-aw/agent/. Use a pre-agent step to redirect the step
summary file: create a real file at /tmp/gh-aw/agent/step-summary.md and symlink
/tmp/gh-aw/agent-step-summary.md to it. The agent writes to the agent-writable
path, and the post-agent append_agent_step_summary.sh follows the symlink to
pick up the content.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Run auto-triage every 10 minutes instead of 30

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

 Only include fields that have non-null values in the triage JSON. Omit any field where the source value is null or absent.
+
+## Step 4 — Upload triage reports and write step summary
+
+Copy the three triage output files into `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/` so they are included in the workflow's `agent` artifact, then write the Markdown report to the step summary so it's visible on the Actions run page without downloading artifacts.
+
+```bash
+cp output/ai/repos/mono-SkiaSharp/ai-triage/${{ needs.pre_activation.outputs.issue_number }}.json /tmp/gh-aw/agent/
+cp output/ai/repos/mono-SkiaSharp/ai-triage/${{ needs.pre_activation.outputs.issue_number }}.md /tmp/gh-aw/agent/
+cp output/ai/repos/mono-SkiaSharp/ai-triage/${{ needs.pre_activation.outputs.issue_number }}.html /tmp/gh-aw/agent/

+
+All three files MUST be copied and the markdown MUST be appended to `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/step-summary.md`. Verify they exist before finishing.

data persistence. Resolves the data-key from a workflow name mapping

- Schedule changed from every 10m to daily
- persist-triage.py writes to output/ai-triage/{number}/triage.json
- auto-triage.md copies to /tmp/gh-aw/agent/ai-triage/{number}/
- All path references updated across SKILL.md, evals, references

ci: regroup and rename GitHub Actions workflows; prune dead ones (#4260)

[CI] Regroup and rename GitHub Actions workflows; prune dead ones (#4260)

The Actions sidebar sorts alphabetically by workflow `name`, so shared
prefixes are the only thing that visually groups related workflows. Only
the `Docs - *` set was grouped; everything else was scattered. This PR
renames workflows into three intent-based groups, removes long-disabled
superseded ones, and fixes every place that references a workflow by name.

Groups:

  * Pages - * (was Docs - *; this is the GitHub Pages/site infra, not API
    docs): Deploy, Go Live!, PR Staging - Cleanup, PR Staging - Sweep Stale
  * PR - * (event-driven PR helpers): Backport, Rebase, Artifacts Comment
  * Sync - * (scheduled commit-back / sync bots): Skia Upstream, Docs
    Submodule, Release Notes & API Diffs, Agentic Data, Issue Triage, Samples

`Manage NuGet Feed` and `Copilot Setup Steps` stay standalone (the latter
keeps its exact name — GitHub special-cases it).

Renaming a workflow is not just the `name:` line: `workflow_run` triggers
and our tooling reference workflows *by name*, so those references are
updated in lockstep to avoid silently breaking the chained automation:

  * build-site-go-live.yml `workflow_run` -> Pages names
  * persist-aw-data.yml `workflow_run` trigger *and* its `resolve_key`
    case -> `Sync - Issue Triage`
  * recompiled the three gh-aw `*.lock.yml` files from their `.md` sources
    via `gh aw compile` (name-only diffs; never hand-edited)
  * .agents/skills/ci-status/* (dashboard `GITHUB_WORKFLOWS` map, tables,
    severity lists, sample output) and release-publish/SKILL.md, which call
    `gh workflow run` by name
  * documentation/dev/writing-docs.md and maintaining.md prose

Removed four superseded, already-disabled workflows — issue triage and
labeling are now handled by the agentic `Sync - Issue Triage`:

  * similarissues.yml, label-with-ai.yml, triage-and-repro.yml,
    engagement-scores.yml

Historical entries under documentation/docfx/releases/* are left unchanged
on purpose — they record past PR titles and are an immutable changelog.

Note: several "ghost" workflows (deleted files whose run history kept them
in the UI) were cleared separately by deleting their run history, since
GitHub has no delete button for a fileless workflow.

[skills] Add perf/* label taxonomy and rework memory-leak-fixer focus areas (#4362)

[skills] Add perf/* label taxonomy and rework memory-leak-fixer focus areas (#4362)

Two related improvements to the agentic-workflow skills. Memory-leak
findings previously landed with only the `agentic-workflows` label — a
label read by nothing and present on zero issues/PRs — so leaks and
performance reports had no meaningful classification, and the triage
skill had no rule mapping either to a quality tenet.

~~ perf/* label taxonomy ~~

There is no dedicated "memory-leak" label, and grouping every speed,
memory, or size concern under the single `tenet/performance` umbrella
loses the sub-type. Add a `perf/*` axis beneath that umbrella, grounded
in the repo's real corpus (61 tenet/performance + ~25 memory-leak
issues): perf/memory-leak, perf/allocations, perf/interop,
perf/rendering, perf/throughput, perf/startup, perf/size. Any perf/*
implies tenet/performance.

  * memory-leak-fixer workflow: drop agentic-workflows; label the
    finding issue and fix PR with tenet/performance + perf/memory-leak.
  * issue-triage skill: add the perf axis to labels.md, the schema
    (classifiedPerf enum + validated perf[] field), the cheatsheet,
    SKILL.md, and the report template.
  * auto-triage workflow: apply classification.perf[] labels; raise the
    add-labels cap 10 -> 12 to fit the new axis.

Type classification (type/bug vs type/enhancement) is left to triage on
purpose — a leak is usually a bug, but a "make it faster" report may be
an enhancement.

~~ "family" -> "focus area" rework ~~

Align the memory-leak-fixer's vocabulary with the new performance-fixer
skill (#4361), which routes over "focus areas" and a focus_area knob.
The 11 rotating leak categories are now focus areas rather than
families, and the workflow's focus_family dispatch input is renamed to
focus_area. The single overarching "leak family" becomes "class of
leaks" so the term is dropped entirely. Terminology only — no
behavioural change.

Both .lock.yml files were regenerated with `gh aw compile` (0 errors);
the perf/* labels were created in mono/SkiaSharp.
